It is considered a shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}, and its {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was formerly that of a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. There is also a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiratori Shrine}} in Teramachi, Toyama City (ranked as a former village shrine), which is said to be related to this shrine. Additionally, {{ill|Kumano shrine|es|Santuario kumano|fr|Kumano-jinja|it|Santuario kumano|ja|熊野神社|simple|Kumano shrine|tr|Kumano tapınağı|qid=Q3200355}} in Tomosaka, Fuchū-machi of the same city is identified as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} (candidate shrine). {{nihongo|'''Shiratori Shrine (Toyama)'''|白鳥神社 (富山市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899|lt=Etchū Province}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}
* It has also been proposed that {{ill|Amenohiboko|fa|آمه‌نوهیبوکو|fr|Amenohiboko|id|Amenohiboko|ja|アメノヒボコ|ko|아메노히보코|zh|天日槍|qid=Q713100|lt=Hiboko}} is enshrined here<ref>Suzuka (1902), p. 518</ref>.

== History ==
There is a theory that the shrine was founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}} (192–200). According to the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}', in the 11th month of the first year of Emperor Chūai (192), the emperor, longing for the divine spirit of his father {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}, who had become a white bird, ordered provinces throughout the country to present white birds. As a result, on the intercalary 11th month, 4th day, four white birds were presented from {{ill|Koshi Province (Japan)|de|Provinz Koshi (Japan)|es|Provincia de Koshi (Japón)|ff|Koshi Province (Japan)|fr|Province de Koshi (Japon)|ja|越国|ko|고시국|nl|Koshi (provincie)|pt|Província de Koshi|simple|Koshi Province (Japan)|zh|越國 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Kosi-kok|zh_yue|越國 (日本)|qid=Q1351611}}, and it is said that the white birds from this locality in Etchū Province were among those presented.

Although the exact date of the shrine’s founding is unknown, it is identified with the '''Shiratori Shrine''' listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' as a {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}} {{ill|Nei District, Toyama|ja|婦負郡|ko|네이군|zh|婦負郡|qid=Q6987940}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=minor national shrine (Kokuhei-shōsha)}}.
